## transfer_to_human (Phase 5.6 -- new)
`POST /webhook/transfer-to-human`

**Body:** `business_id`, `call_id`, `caller_number`, `transfer_reason`

Decides whether this business has an approved human line to transfer to, for one of a fixed set of universal reasons (`explicit_human_request`, `emergency_or_distress`, `complaint`, `payment_dispute`, `unknown_or_sensitive_question` -- matching config/business-profile.example.json's transfer_rules.universal_triggers). Returns an approved transfer instruction (this business's own transfer_number) or, if none is configured yet, a safe callback fallback -- it never invents or assumes a transfer destination, and never approves a reason outside the fixed set.

Logs the decision to call_events (event_type: 'transfer_triggered', event_data: { reason, decision } only -- no phone numbers, no names, no transfer number) when call_id already matches a calls row for this business. transfer_to_human typically fires mid-call, before log_call has created that row, so a logged: "call_not_found" response is the normal case, not a failure -- the transfer reason should still land in that call's eventual log_call call_summary.

TRUST MODEL CAVEAT (see docs/n8n-setup.md "Tenant isolation"): like every workflow here, this resolves business_id by trusting the caller-supplied string and looking it up against businesses.business_slug. That keeps one business's data out of another's response in this local demo, but it is NOT production tenant isolation -- nothing here cryptographically verifies the caller is the real Vapi assistant for that business. Production hardening (Vapi-to-n8n request authentication, and resolving business_id server-side from the inbound phone number/assistant rather than trusting a caller-supplied field) is a later live-integration task, not done in this phase.

This phase does not touch Vapi, Exotel, Twilio, deployment, or any live credentials.
